input_note: Neither input is raw points. The VFE takes the 10-channel per-point expansion (raw point, offset from the pillar centroid, offset from the pillar centre) that BCDL's pillarPointFeatures() builds; the backbone takes the BEV scatter canvas built from the VFE's output. Both are `no_preprocess` featuremaps. Points must be in the lidar frame KITTI was recorded in.

outputs.cls: 1x18x248x216 anchor scores (3 classes x 2 rotations, sigmoid on the host)
outputs.box: 1x42x248x216 box residuals (7 per anchor, decoded against the anchor grid on the host)
outputs.dir: 1x12x248x216 direction-bin logits (2 bins per anchor; without them every heading is correct only modulo pi)
outputs.note: The anchor decode and BEV NMS are host-side in BCDL, deliberately — see graph_rewrites.

quantisation: compiler default (no optimization directive) — predominantly int8, for BOTH graphs. Measured, not assumed: set_all_nodes_int16 on the VFE scores WORSE (0.9567 vs int8's 0.9988 against the float ONNX) while saving 0.26 ms.

licence.tier: C — recipe only, no redistributable binary
licence.detail: OpenPCDet's code is Apache-2.0, but the checkpoint is trained on KITTI, and KITTI's terms are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Under the weights-chain rule the .hbm inherits the non-commercial restriction from the data it was trained on, so this repo ships the recipe and BCDL ships the runtime; neither ships the binary. The D-Robotics zoo's own prebuilt PointPillars stages carry the same restriction and are redistributed by the vendor, not by us.

toolchain.note: The host HBDK and the board HBRT must match; 3.7.0 host pairs with 4.0.5 board.

cosine.note: B is the VFE .hbm against its own float ONNX on a real sweep, de-strided (see traps). C is the whole board chain against the same chain run in onnxruntime — cls 0.9994, box 0.9745, dir 0.9584. Scoring against the PUBLISHED chain instead would be meaningless: it is different weights, so the comparison mixes the checkpoint change into the int8 cost and reads as more favourable than it is.

task_metric.name: 3-D boxes on a real KITTI sweep: against the chain's own float, and against the point cloud
task_metric.protocol: Run the exported ONNX pair in onnxruntime and the compiled pair on the board on the SAME sweep, decode both with the same host decoder (BCDL decode_det3d + BEV NMS), and compare box sets. Separately require every box to sit on actual returns, with a range-dependent floor. Comparing against the PUBLISHED chain instead is not a quantisation measurement: it is different weights.
task_metric.threshold: board box count within 1 of float's at threshold 0.3; matched centres under 0.2 m; >= 90% of the anchors float scores above 0.3 still above it on the board
task_metric.measured: board 18 boxes vs float 18; matched centres 0.070 m mean / 0.136 m max; scores 0.035 low on average; 169 of 181 (93%) of float's >0.3 anchors survive; 1 heading flipped by pi. Point support 552-3212 per box inside 20 m; the furthest box (62 m) has 8, which is what a car at 62 m looks like. Against the published chain: 18 boxes vs its 16, 13 of the 18 same class within 1 m — that residual is the checkpoint, not the quantisation.
task_metric.note: Standing check in BCDL as tests/test_lidar_board_py.py, which runs against whichever chain is installed. NOT measured: KITTI mAP. These are single-sweep fidelity figures, answering whether the board reproduces the float model rather than how good the detector is.

measured.note: S100P, hrt_model_exec perf, thread_num 1, min of 3 runs on a quiet board; spread under 1%. Latencies are the two graphs of this recipe; the comparison is the published three-stage chain. The 8-sweep calibration costs nothing in latency or size versus the 1-sweep build it replaced.

end_to_end_ms.note: Through BCDL, including host voxelize / expansion / scatter / decode. Of the 43 ms, 8.8 is BPU and about 17 is host-to-device copying — 12 of that the 55 MB BEV canvas.

rejected_builds.name: the published VFE layout, (11546, 32, 4)
rejected_builds.why: 290 ms for a 4->64 MLP of about 95 MFLOP — roughly 0.3 GFLOPS. Layout-bound, not compute-bound: a huge pillar axis against a 4-wide channel axis is the worst shape a convolution engine can be handed. The same arithmetic over (1, 10, P, 32) is 1.62 ms.

rejected_builds.name: set_all_nodes_int16 on the VFE
rejected_builds.why: Worse AND barely faster: 0.9567 against the float reference vs int8's 0.9988, at 1.36 ms vs 1.62 ms. The compiler's own per-layer report says the same (conv 0.9926 vs 0.9999). This is the opposite of the usual int8/int16 trade and is the reason the config carries no optimization directive.

rejected_builds.name: drop-in replacement of the published VFE only
rejected_builds.why: The published .hbm is not this checkpoint. Best-matching-channel median correlation is 0.904 but only 3 of 64 channels exceed 0.99 and the identity-order correlation is 0.000, so the channel ordering differs. All three stages have to be replaced together, which is why the backbone and head are re-exported here too.

rejected_builds.name: single-frame calibration for the backbone+head
rejected_builds.why: It compiles clean and loses 4 of 18 boxes. Against the chain's own float: box cosine 0.897 and dir 0.848 (vs 0.9745 / 0.9584 with 8 sweeps), scores depressed 0.135, only 81% of float's >0.3 anchors surviving, and 2 headings flipped by pi. Lowering the score threshold does NOT recover them — board/float goes 14/18 at 0.30 and 24/34 at 0.15, so the gap widens: what degrades is the ranking, not a bias. Eight sweeps fix it at identical latency and file size.

graph_rewrites.op: PillarVFE (linear + BN + ReLU + max over points) -> 1x1 Conv + MaxPool over (1, 10, P, 32)
graph_rewrites.why: Layout. The per-point MLP becomes a channel convolution and the max over points becomes a pooling window; the 10-channel expansion moves to the host. 290 ms -> 1.62 ms.
graph_rewrites.verified: The compiled graph scores 0.9988 against the float ONNX on a real sweep, de-strided. Isolated: feeding the board head the FLOAT canvas gives the same error as the whole chain (0.9994/0.9745/0.9584 either way), so the VFE's contribution to the chain's error is negligible and the head is where the quantisation cost lives.

graph_rewrites.op: AnchorHeadSingle -> cut at conv_cls / conv_box / conv_dir_cls; decode on the host
graph_rewrites.why: The published head bakes anchor decoding in with ScatterND, which compiles without a warning into a model whose output columns are never written — the same silent failure as YOLOP in this repo.
graph_rewrites.verified: Cut, the head compiles at cls cosine 1.000000 and box 0.999946. BCDL's generateAnchors3d reproduces the published graph's own anchor constants to 7.6e-06, which is how the ordering was established (class-major then rotation, a CLOSED linspace over the range, and anchor z as the centre rather than the base) rather than guessed.

graph_rewrites.op: backbone_2d + the cut head exported as one graph
graph_rewrites.why: Once the head is three 1x1 convolutions it may as well ride along: one Engine and one round trip. 113.7 ms -> 7.20 ms, which is more than fusion alone explains — the published backbone is a nash-e int16 build and this one is nash-m int8.
graph_rewrites.verified: export.py asserts the head geometry (18/42/12 at 248x216) against the published one before writing the ONNX.

rebuild.note: This recipe was re-run end to end (export -> calib -> compile) rather than transcribed, on 2026-08-12 with OE 3.7.0, and its output REPLACED the earlier builds on the board.
rebuild.vfe: 15756160 bytes. Calibrated on 8 real KITTI sweeps; input threshold 69.094, output 13.872, compiler-reported output cosine 0.999185.
rebuild.bbhead: 35153704 bytes, calibrated on the same 8 sweeps.
rebuild.why_it_matters: The first builds calibrated on one frame. See rejected_builds — that is where 4 of 18 boxes went.

board_verification.note: Both graphs compiled from this recipe, run on an S100P, and validated against the chain's own float and against the point cloud (see task_metric). Latency min-of-3 on a quiet board, unchanged by the calibration fix (1.63 / 7.20 ms). What was NOT done: KITTI mAP.
board_verification.trap: The VFE's output is stride-padded — [1,64,11546,1] pads each channel by 6 float slots — so reading the device buffer flat displaces channel c by 6c and the last channel by 378 pillars. That scores 0.70 against the float reference and looks like a quantisation failure; it is a reader bug. De-strided, the board matches the compiler's own reported 0.956701 bit for bit on the int16 build. BCDL's Engine.infer() gathers padded outputs since the fix, but anyone reading outputData() directly must honour outputStride().
